claims.text: DonHangApp is a StatelessWidget whose build returns a MaterialApp with home: ProductListScreen(apiClient: apiClient); its comment describes it as composing the app shell from small widgets.
ProductListScreen, LoginScreen and CreateOrderScreen are separate widgets in separate files under lib/screens, each with a constructor requiring only an ApiClient.
In ProductListScreen, each product row is an inline ListTile(title: Text(product.name), trailing: Text(price)) inside ListView.builder's itemBuilder, using only product.
There is no ProductTile class in DonHang.App at stage-1.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: git grep ProductTile (no match in DonHang.App/lib)

claims.text: A StatelessWidget subclass with a final Product field and a build returning the same ListTile can replace the inline ListTile, producing the same screen.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: StatelessWidget; refs/flutter-website ui (building widgets)

claims.text: Flutter's docs recommend splitting large build methods into smaller widgets.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/best-practices.md (split large widgets into smaller ones)

claims.text: SRP applied to widgets: one widget, one reason to change; a widget's constructor parameters are its contract.
